clinical_knowledge.topic: Drug-Induced Liver Injury (Herbal Supplement) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Drug-Induced Liver Injury (Herbal Supplement) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Immediately discontinue herbal supplement and non-essential medications, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: yellow eyes, dark urine, and severe fatigue for 5 days

Key HPI features: 5-day history of profound lethargy, nausea, loss of appetite, dark tea-coloured urine, and pale clay-coloured stools. Noticed her sclerae and skin turning yellow 2 days ago. Started taking a high-dose herbal weight-loss supplement and paracetamol for headaches 3 weeks prior.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals, mental status (check alertness/flapping tremor for acute liver failure). Abdominal exam: tender hepatomegaly. Bloods: LFTs (markedly elevated ALT/AST >1000 suggests hepatocellular necrosis), bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, INR/coagulation screen, viral hepatitis panel (HAV, HBV, HCV, HEV), paracetamol level.
Relevant background/PMH: mild asthma, no prior hepatic illness or blood transfusions
Current medications: salbutamol inhaler PRN, recently started 'SlimPlus' herbal extracts (containing green tea extract and unknown botanicals), paracetamol 1g PRN
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Drug-Induced Liver Injury (Herbal Supplement).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Paracetamol hepatotoxicity without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Any confusion or altered mental state — suggests acute liver failure.
management_principles: Immediately discontinue herbal supplement and non-essential medications
N-acetylcysteine (NAC) consideration if acute liver failure or paracetamol toxicity suspected
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 41F with 5-day history of profound lethargy, nausea, loss of appetite, dark tea-coloured urine, and pale clay-coloured stools. Noticed her sclerae and skin turning yellow 2 days ago. Started taking a high-dose herbal weight-loss supplement and paracetamol for headaches 3 weeks prior.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals, mental status (check alertness/flapping tremor for acute liver failure). Abdominal exam: tender hepatomegaly. Bloods: LFTs (markedly elevated ALT/AST >1000 suggests hepatocellular necrosis), bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, INR/coagulation screen, viral hepatitis panel (HAV, HBV, HCV, HEV), paracetamol level.
reference_soap.assessment: Drug-Induced Liver Injury (DILI) likely secondary to herbal weight-loss supplement vs acute viral hepatitis. DDx: paracetamol hepatotoxicity, autoimmune hepatitis, biliary obstruction.
reference_soap.plan: Immediately discontinue herbal supplement and non-essential medications. N-acetylcysteine (NAC) consideration if acute liver failure or paracetamol toxicity suspected. Monitor INR and glucose closely. Hepatology consult and report adverse event to drug regulatory body.

learning_objectives: Perform a comprehensive exposure history including over-the-counter drugs, herbal remedies, and supplements
Distinguish hepatocellular injury from cholestatic jaundice based on clinical symptoms and lab profiles
Identify early warning signs of acute liver failure (coagulopathy, hepatic encephalopathy, hypoglycaemia)
Address patient anxiety regarding liver toxicity and transplant risk

teaching.one_liner: A toxic reaction to a medication or herbal supplement injures the liver cells, causing jaundice, dark urine, and pale stools within days to weeks of starting it.
red_flags: Any confusion or altered mental state — suggests acute liver failure

must_ask.say: Can you tell me exactly what's in the weight-loss supplement, and when you started taking it?
How much paracetamol have you been taking, and how often?
Have you noticed your skin turning yellow, or your stools going pale?
Do you drink alcohol, and if so, how much?
Have you traveled recently, used injectable drugs, or had unprotected sex?
Has anyone noticed you seeming more confused or forgetful lately?

history.answer: Doctor, my eyes have turned yellow and my urine looks like dark tea over the last few days, and I feel completely exhausted.
I began feeling horribly tired and nauseated five days ago, and then two days ago I noticed my eyes and skin turning yellow.
My urine has turned very dark, almost like strong black tea or cola.
My bowel movements have looked pale and grayish-white, like clay, for the past four days.
Yes, my skin has been moderately itchy all over for the past couple of days.
I have a mild, dull ache and heavy feeling in the upper right side of my stomach, but no sharp cramps after meals.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or night sweats.
My head feels clear and I'm not confused, but I feel so drained that I've been sleeping a lot more than usual.
No, I haven't noticed any unusual bruising, bleeding gums, or bloody nose.
I've felt really sick to my stomach and haven't had any appetite to eat since this started five days ago.
No unintentional weight loss. In fact, I've been actively dieting and trying to lose weight.
No, I don't feel lightheaded, dizzy, or short of breath.
About three weeks ago, I started taking an herbal supplement called SlimPlus that contains concentrated green tea extracts to help me lose weight.
I've taken one-gram tablets of paracetamol here and there for headaches over the last three weeks, but never more than two or three times a week and never an overdose.
No, I haven't eaten any raw oysters, shellfish, or undercooked seafood.
No, nobody at home or work has been sick or had yellow eyes.
I don't have hepatitis B or C as far as I know, and I received the standard hepatitis vaccines years ago.
No, I have never had a blood transfusion, and I don't have any tattoos or body piercings.
No, I have never injected drugs or used any recreational drugs.
No, I've never been diagnosed with gallstones and have never had surgery on my gallbladder.
No, my belly doesn't look bloated or swollen, and my ankles aren't puffy.
I'm worried that the SlimPlus herbal pills I bought on the internet are toxic and poisoned my liver.
I'm terrified that my liver is failing and that I might end up needing an urgent liver transplant.
I want you to check my blood right away to see how bad my liver is, and give me an antidote or medicine to clear out the toxins.
I have mild asthma, but no history of liver disease or other medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and I've never stayed in a hospital.
I use a blue salbutamol inhaler only when my asthma flares up, which is rare, plus the SlimPlus herbal pills and occasional paracetamol.
I don't have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used vape products.
I drink very rarely, maybe a single glass of wine at a dinner party once every few months.
I work in an office as an accountant, and I live at home with my partner.
Nobody in my family has had liver disease, jaundice, or autoimmune conditions.
I'm in a long-term, monogamous relationship with my partner.
My last period was about two weeks ago and is regular; my partner had a vasectomy, so there's no chance I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/74 mmHg, heart rate 76 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Appears fatigued and visibly jaundiced with yellowish skin tone, but in no acute distress.
Alert and oriented to person, place, and time; answers questions clearly without cognitive slowing.
No asterixis or flapping tremor noted on outstretched hands with wrists dorsiflexed.
Marked scleral icterus bilaterally; conjunctivae are pink without pallor.
Generalized yellowing of the skin with a few excoriation marks from scratching; no spider nevi or palmar erythema.
Mild tenderness on palpation in the right upper quadrant; no guarding or rigidity.
Negative Murphy's sign with no sharp arrest of inspiration on deep right subcostal palpation.
Smooth, tender liver edge palpable 2 to 3 cm below the right costal margin; spleen is not palpable.
Tympanitic abdomen throughout with no shifting dullness or detectable fluid wave.
No pitting edema in either lower extremity.
